Shajahan Siraj’s Liberation War role remembered on 6th death anniversary
2026-07-14T17:38:42+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Tangail
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/shajahan-sirajs-liberation-war-role-remembered-6th-death-anniversary-4223631

Speakers at a memorial meeting today said former minister Shajahan Siraj played an important role in the Liberation War as a key organiser and that future generations would remember his contribution to the country's independence.

Dedicated to serving the nation both during the war and in politics, his contribution to the establishment of an independent Bangladesh would be remembered with respect, they said.

The memorial meeting was organised at Kalihati Shajahan Siraj College in Tangail to mark his sixth death anniversary. Siraj, a commander of the Bangladesh Liberation Force, established the college.

Siraj, a veteran politician who read out the manifesto of Bangladesh's independence, died of lung cancer in 2020.

Tangail-4 (Kalihati) lawmaker Lutfar Rahman Matin attended the programme as the chief guest, while Barrister Sarwat Siraj Shukla, president of the Shajahan Siraj College Governing Council and Siraj's daughter, presided over the event.

Rabeya Siraj, Siraj's widow, donor member of the college and a representative of the governing council, spoke as the main discussant.

Siraj was known as one of the "four caliphs" of the Liberation War alongside ASM Abdur Rob, Abdul Kuddus Makhon and Nur-e-Alam Siddique.

In independent Bangladesh, he served as minister for environment and forest from 2001 to 2006. He was also a former vice-chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

Born in Tangail on March 1, 1943, Siraj entered politics through the movement against the Hamidur Rahman Education Commission in 1962 while he was a student at Sadat College in Karatia, Tangail.
